analysis.title: GS Duttenhoefer - Duttenhoefer's Daily 30.10.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 -30bps at 7720 (+13% ytd), US 10yr at 4.92%, Brent $116, Gold $3989, Bitcoin $79k. ECB held rates as expected. Only 2 Mag-7 stocks (Apple, Nvidia) are outperforming the S&P ytd.
Amazon fell 7% post market. 3Q26 revenue of $201.9bn (+12% yoy) missed consensus of $202.3bn. AWS growth accelerated to +39%, but free cash flow was -$42.4bn on $77bn of cash capex in the quarter.

Amazon positives: GS says compute demand outstrips supply with capacity largely sold out for the next 2 years, AWS growth is expected at 40%+ in 2027/28, and cost to serve per unit has fallen for the 4th consecutive year.

Amazon negatives: online stores revenue grew only +2% yoy to $68.5bn (lowest since early 2023, vs consensus $69.1bn) and advertising missed ($19.6bn vs consensus $20.8bn) for the first time in 7 quarters. FY26 capex is reaffirmed at about $220bn and management warned FY27 capex will rise meaningfully.
GS keeps a structurally positive view on Amazon in cloud infrastructure and enterprise agentic orchestration. It attributes the near-term multiple compression to the cash flow drag.
Intel fell 23% post market on weak PC demand.

GS's Consumer Experience basket rose 4% yesterday and was the best theme. GS cites accelerating spending on experiences, attractive valuations, revisions close to inflecting and positioning that is not crowded. The basket's exposure to higher-income cohorts has insulated it from higher fuel costs. Basket mix is 40% live entertainment, 20% leisure, 20% hotels, 20% cruises. Visa also cited strong travel demand.
Microsoft is raising $25bn in bonds with maturities of 2 to 40 years, its first US bond sale since 2017.

Middle East: the US warned allies to prepare for possible renewed military action against Iran after next week's midterms. At the same time JD Vance contacted a senior Iranian official with a letter to revive peace talks.

US midterms are next week. GS says the more actionable question is which policy areas become easier to negotiate, get more regulatory attention or gain leverage in spending debates. It lists ACA subsidies, drug pricing, power inflation, government spending and corporate tax.
Binance temporarily suspended all deposits and withdrawals after one of the industry's biggest security breaches, with estimated total impact around $6.3bn.

AI in healthcare: GS sees AI's impact on drug development as broad across molecule design, lab optimization, manufacturing documentation, regulatory drafting and trial planning. It reiterates its bullish AI view and points to the rebalanced 30-stock AI Health Care Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCAIP).
Buybacks: November accounts for roughly 10.1% of yearly buyback spend, the 2nd strongest month after August. Year-to-date repurchase authorizations are $1341bn (+14% yoy).
Fed: GS expects a second and final hike in December. A third hike in March is possible if inflation comes in higher than GS expects.
Reddit management said AI search mode does not drive traffic to them or, as far as they know, to anyone, a fundamental shift from Google being a traffic driver.
Stat of the Day: Fed data show households' direct holdings account for 42% of the US corporate equity market.

market_movers.rationale: GS continues to view Amazon as structurally advantaged in cloud and agentic orchestration. The stock fell 7% post market on capex and negative free cash flow of $42.4bn.

sector_views.rationale: Spending on experiences is accelerating, valuations are attractive, revisions are close to inflecting and positioning is not crowded. Higher-income exposure has insulated the basket from fuel costs.
AI gains appear across drug development steps and GS reiterates its bullish AI view via the rebalanced GSHLCAIP basket.
